problem:
Given that $A,B,$ and $C$ are $6\times 6$ matrices which of the following statements are always true? 

- $A(BC)=(AB)C$
- $A(B-C)=AB-CA$
- $CA=AC$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(-1,0),(1,0),$ and $(0,1).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(1,0)$
- $(-1,0)$
- $(0,2)$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-2-0}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,0),(-1,0),(0,\frac{1}{2}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
